citation: Motley AM, Bright NA, Seaman MN, Robinson MS. Clathrin-mediated endocytosis in AP-2-depleted cells. The Journal of Cell Biology. 2003. doi:10.1083/jcb.200305145.
description: AP-2 mu2 RNAi in HeLaM cells severely inhibited receptor-mediated transferrin uptake while preserving some AP-2-independent cargo entry. This supports an AP-2-complex bridge for Ap2s1 pairs with Tfrc or synaptic/endocytic responses, but it does not establish AP2S1-specific transcript directions.

citation: Ma X, Li L, Li Z, Huang Z, Yang Y, Liu P, Guo D, Li Y, Wu T, Luo R, Xu J, Ye WC, Jiang B, Shi L. eEF2 in the prefrontal cortex promotes excitatory synaptic transmission and social novelty behavior. EMBO Reports. 2022. doi:10.15252/embr.202154543.
description: Eef2 heterozygous mice and mPFC excitatory-neuron knockdown showed reduced protein synthesis, spine density, neuronal excitability, and AMPAR-mediated synaptic transmission. The result provides a neuron-specific bridge from Eef2 loss to synaptic dysfunction, not to a decisive mRNA-signature direction.

citation: Dahlqvist J, Torma H, Badhai J, Dahl N. siRNA silencing of proteasome maturation protein (POMP) activates the unfolded protein response and constitutes a model for KLICK genodermatosis. PLOS ONE. 2012. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0029471.
description: POMP siRNA reduced proteasome subunits and prolonged POMP silencing induced CHOP, consistent with unfolded-protein-response and ER-stress activation in cultured cells. This is direct POMP-loss support for a proteasome-stress bridge in Pomp screen responses.

citation: Brehm A, Liu Y, Sheikh A, Marrero B, Omoyinmi E, Zhou Q, Montealegre G, Biancotto A, Reinhardt A, Almeida de Jesus A, Pelletier M, Tsai WL, Remmers EF, Kardava L, Hill S, Kim H, Lachmann HJ, Megarbane A, Chae JJ, Brady J, Castillo RD, Brown D, Casano AV, Gao L, Chapelle D, Huang Y, Stone D, Chen Y, Sotzny F, Lee CC, Kastner DL, Torrelo A, Zlotogorski A, Moir S, Gadina M, McCoy P, Wesley R, Rother KI, Hildebrand PW, Brogan P, Kruger E, Aksentijevich I, Goldbach-Mansky R. Additive loss-of-function proteasome subunit mutations in CANDLE/PRAAS patients promote type I IFN production. The Journal of Clinical Investigation. 2015. doi:10.1172/JCI81260.
description: This study identified PSMB4 and POMP proteasome-pathway mutations in PRAAS, showed that the mutations variably disrupt proteasome assembly and activity, and recapitulated type-I-interferon induction after siRNA depletion of proteasome subunits. It supports a target-to-proteasome-dysfunction bridge for both Psmb4 and Pomp perturbations.

citation: Adler AS, McCleland ML, Yee S, Yaylaoglu M, Hussain S, Cosino E, Quinones G, Modrusan Z, Seshagiri S, Torres E, Chopra VS, Haley B, Zhang Z, Blackwood EM, Singh M, Junttila M, Stephan JP, Liu J, Pau G, Fearon ER, Jiang Z, Firestein R. An integrative analysis of colon cancer identifies an essential function for PRPF6 in tumor growth. Genes & Development. 2014. doi:10.1101/gad.237206.113.
description: PRPF6, a U4/U6.U5 tri-snRNP spliceosome component, was inhibited in cancer cells and reduced PRPF6 altered constitutive and alternative splicing in transcriptome analyses. The paper gives a direct PRPF6-to-splicing bridge but not the neuronal gene-expression directions measured here.

citation: Bai B, Hales CM, Chen PC, Gozal Y, Dammer EB, Fritz JJ, Wang X, Xia Q, Duong DM, Street C, Cantero G, Cheng D, Jones DR, Wu Z, Li Y, Diner I, Heilman CJ, Rees HD, Wu H, Lin L, Szulwach KE, Gearing M, Mufson EJ, Bennett DA, Montine TJ, Seyfried NT, Wingo TS, Sun YE, Jin P, Hanfelt J, Willcock DM, Levey A, Lah JJ, Peng J. U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein complex and RNA splicing alterations in Alzheimer's disease. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America. 2013. doi:10.1073/pnas.1310249110.
description: The paper linked human brain U1-snRNP accumulation, including U1-70K, with dysregulated RNA processing and found that U1-70K knockdown or U1-snRNP inhibition increased APP protein. It supplies a biologically specific but incomplete SNRNP70/U1-snRNP bridge to RNA-processing phenotypes.

citation: Rajanala K, Nandicoori VK. Localization of nucleoporin Tpr to the nuclear pore complex is essential for Tpr mediated regulation of the export of unspliced RNA. PLOS ONE. 2012. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0029921.
description: Tpr knockdown in mammalian cells enhanced cytoplasmic export of an unspliced reporter RNA, implicating nuclear-pore-localized Tpr and Nup153 in intron-containing RNA retention, processing, or degradation. This directly connects Tpr loss to RNA surveillance but not to the exact neuronal transcript changes.

citation: Yap K, Lim ZQ, Khandelia P, Friedman B, Makeyev EV. Coordinated regulation of neuronal mRNA steady-state levels through developmentally controlled intron retention. Genes & Development. 2012. doi:10.1101/gad.188037.112.
description: This study showed that intron-containing synaptic transcripts are retained and degraded in nonneuronal cells and that clearance requires nuclear RNA surveillance components including Tpr and the exosome. It provides a neuronal-transcript-specific but developmental and indirect bridge for Tpr perturbation phenotypes.
